title: Zero-divisor criteria for absolute concentration robustness
summary: García Puente et al. (arXiv:2401.00078v3, Question 3.13) asked whether a unique positive zero-divisor value is necessary or sufficient for absolute concentration robustness (ACR) in at-most-bimolecular mass-action networks. Explicit networks with positive rational rates answer both questions negatively. A further three-species example shows that their candidate algorithm can miss a zero-divisor ACR value under an admissible elimination order, refuting the unrestricted elimination-order form of Conjecture 4.7.
